assets.name: 包厢俯观
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Produce ONE finished fine-art scenic illustration, wide landscape 16:9, for a concept called MIRAGE SUN THEATRE. No text, no interface, no titles.

CORE IDEA MUST BE VISIBLE: the theatre itself is an inhabitable three-dimensional instrument for telling stories. A suspended optical LIGHTING SYSTEM called the Mirage Sun illuminates different plays, and each play becomes a distinct physical world on the stage. The worlds have volume, floors, suspended objects, stairs and actual depth, not landscapes printed on flat panels. The impression of a kaleidoscope comes from a few large angled scenic mirrors reflecting real parts of those worlds, recombining fragments as the viewer changes position.

VIEW 01: from an UPPER LEFT PRIVATE BALCONY, looking down diagonally across the entire deep opera stage at about 30 degrees, a cinematic off-axis three-quarter perspective, never symmetrical or frontal. Foreground lower left has a close dark curved balcony rail and one cropped velvet curtain, establishing the viewer's position. The right curved horseshoe balconies and stage pit reveal substantial architectural depth. The theatre has quiet ivory plaster, deep aubergine and midnight-blue silk, a few broad thin champagne metal ribs. Precise elegant proportions, selectively ornamented cornices, not a baroque palace covered in gold.

The HERO is an extraordinary suspended stage-light apparatus in the upper middle: a luminous warm-white porcelain SOLAR LANTERN with a thin architectural halo, two smaller offset optical 'false suns' created in its lenses. It is visibly engineered, held by a graceful brass overhead yoke and narrow cables attached to the theatre grid, not a sun or moon painted in the sky. Three large clean optical vanes around it split broad soft-edged sheets of light down into three story worlds. Clearly show continuous light paths from lantern through vanes to stage scenery, with subtle restrained spectral colour at crossings.

On the deep stepped stage BELOW, three different plays are simultaneously becoming real, connected through an oblique sequence of wings and clear gaps:
NEAR LEFT an icy pale-lilac abyss with a tiny broken bridge, translucent glacier masses rise out of a low stage trap, no buildings;
FAR CENTRE an indigo astronomical harbour of floating circular landings, one vast delicate brass orbital instrument, tiny towers and hanging planetary forms, not a gothic city;
RIGHT a jade primordial grove with monumental roots, orange leaves and a levitating rocky island with a cloud waterfall, deep organic forms contrasting the icy angular landscape.
The forest is partly seen directly and partly reflected in the back of a large angled mirror; the icy bridge appears as one restrained unexpected reflected fragment over the star harbour. These are optical relationships, not three separate picture windows. Reveal stage edges, little service stairs, overlap, shadows and suspension so the whole theatre is spatially convincing. Three magnificent worlds but only one decisive focal light system. Empty quiet dark space occupies roughly a quarter of the image, giving the luminous theatrical world room to breathe. No audience or people.

ART DIRECTION: a museum-quality contemporary scenographer's painting, fine gouache and tempera glazing on warm textured board combined with a carefully built painted-silk maquette; exceptionally designed luminous pigment, tactile matte surfaces, crafted light and believable deep shadows. Sophisticated dreamlike colour, cultured and strange, large material fields and edited detail. Illustrative painterly architectural perspective, not an architectural wireframe or technical diagram. No glossy game environment, no plastic CGI, no magic particle sparkle, no jewel-encrusted ornament, no rainbow lasers, no repetition of identical arches, no huge literal book, no flying pages. The theatre and solar lighting instrument must dominate the composition and remain recognizable at thumbnail size.

assets.name: 侧台折界
assets.referenceRole: 第一张仅作为剧场建筑、灯具和美术语言的参考，重新生成视角与构图
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a NEW finished wide 16:9 theatrical artwork, VIEW 02 of MIRAGE SUN THEATRE. The attached image is a REFERENCE FOR THE SAME THEATRE ARCHITECTURE, MATERIAL LANGUAGE, THREE STORY WORLDS AND THE MIRAGE SUN LIGHTING SYSTEM ONLY. It is NOT the target composition. Change the camera and visual composition decisively.

NEW CAMERA: eye-level from DEEP INSIDE THE RIGHT STAGE WING, looking sharply DIAGONALLY ACROSS the depth of the theatre. Very strong near-to-far spatial recession, intimate theatrical view, not a symmetrical frontal vista, not a balcony overview. Crop a close dark aubergine velvet leg and the edge of a single angled optical mirror into the extreme RIGHT foreground. On the far LEFT, the ivory horseshoe balconies and quiet unoccupied auditorium are visible beyond the oblique edge of the proscenium, making clear we are ON the stage. A broad stage floor and service steps connect near and far scenery.

The MIRAGE SUN LIGHTING SYSTEM is the recognizable same suspended warm-white porcelain solar globe in a slim brass overhead yoke, with its two smaller lateral false-sun optics. It hangs above the deep middle of the stage, large enough to be read clearly, plainly connected by rigging to the stage grid. A graceful optical lighting instrument, not a random celestial sun in a sky. Its directed light passes through a few thin large angled optical vanes, with physically continuous restrained light sheets down to scenery.

Make the KALEIDOSCOPIC PERCEPTION much more evident and elegant: exactly THREE large tilted mirror/silk scenic facets at different depths along the diagonal, with only fine champagne-coloured edges. They reflect different fragments of the SAME THREE fully physical story worlds, overlapping unexpected edges: in the nearest mirror a glacier bridge appears behind jade tree roots; a far facet catches part of the astronomical ring in an icy canyon; the actual worlds continue in depth outside those mirror edges. Reflected and direct vistas differ visibly. No fractured-mirror confetti, no repeated identically framed pictures.
The nearest world is a mineral-jade and warm-coral giant root grove rising out of a stepped scenic platform, one cloud waterfall spilling toward the orchestra void. The middle world is a deep indigo floating observatory with one enormous delicate orbital ring and suspended circular harbour landings. The far world is silver-lilac broken glacier with tiny abyss bridge and no buildings. Each universe has an utterly different silhouette and spatial law. Show deep landscape volumes, exposed stage edges, suspension and shadow; no flat printed panorama triptych.

ART DIRECTION: premium painted scenic maquette / fine tempera and gouache architectural illustration, keep the reference's dreamlike atmospheric sense and edited classic opera architecture. Strengthen tactile matte pigment, silk, thin metal and paper-like scenic edges, reduce photographic slickness. Use deep quiet indigo/aubergine foreground, luminous ivory lantern, cool violet ice, muted jade, restrained coral. Keep roughly one quarter quiet negative space. Refined asymmetric composition, few deliberate details, rich light rather than clutter. No text, no UI, no books, no logos, no sparkling particles, no gaudy gold foliage everywhere, no neon rainbow lasers, no plastic videogame CGI. This is an individual work of theatrical art about different stories becoming different worlds under a common light.

assets.name: 台口入境
assets.referenceRole: 第一张仅作为剧场建筑、灯具和美术语言的参考，重新生成视角与构图
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a NEW finished wide 16:9 fine-art scenic illustration, VIEW 03 of MIRAGE SUN THEATRE. Attached reference establishes the SAME grand opera theatre, its material palette, three story worlds and signature optical solar-light apparatus. Borrow these identities only; do not copy the camera or arrangement.

NEW CAMERA: a LOW VIEW FROM VERY CLOSE TO THE FRONT STAGE APRON, looking UP AND DIAGONALLY toward the left rear fly tower, approximately a wide 28mm architectural perspective without fisheye distortion. The rounded stage lip occupies one restrained dark foreground curve; a cropped ivory proscenium pier at the LEFT and sharply foreshortened stage floor give emphatic three-dimensional theatre depth. Only a glimpse of curved balcony and upper curtain is visible along far right. The scene should feel like entering the world of a play, not looking at a distant framed painting. Clear diagonal depth, dramatic but elegant.

The MIRAGE SUN is clearly the theatrical LIGHTING SYSTEM: a huge warm-white porcelain optical solar lantern in a slim champagne-metal yoke with two slightly offset companion lens globes, suspended from the upper fly grid in the upper LEFT-CENTRE. From this close low viewpoint its illuminated rings and broad beams appear physically monumental. Stage rigging and bracket are visible and beautifully edited, so it cannot be mistaken for an ordinary moon or background sun. Three large thin translucent optical folds descend obliquely from it. Soft light passes through and divides, actually connects to the different worlds.

The KALEIDOSCOPE unfolds in depth around the viewer as real theatre scenery rather than three framed landscape panels:
at LEFT a silver-lilac broken glacier with deep crevasses and impossibly thin bridge, enormous icy forms rise behind the near stage pier;
in the MIDDLE/REAR an indigo star-sea observatory, enormous brass orbital geometry arches across floating harbour platforms suspended at different elevations;
at RIGHT a giant sculptural jade root system rises from low stage levels, supporting coral-leaf branches and a levitating rocky island with a cloud waterfall.
Two or three extremely large angled semi-mirrored scenic planes intersect these vistas, showing precise unexpected reflections of the icy bridge in the garden and a ring segment over the glacier. The light at those crossings produces a few subtle muted violet, apricot and celadon colour changes. Worlds have deep visible space beyond the optical planes, a single integrated theatrical volume with overlap and occlusion. Leave some shadows quiet; there is one clear focal light and an expressive composition, not an inventory of effects.

A cultured, richly atmospheric contemporary scenographer's painting: delicate matte gouache / tempera glaze over tactile model scenery, believable fabric and hand-painted wood, thin architectural metal, poetic dramatic light with sophisticated shadows. Strong near/far scale, fine painting in the focal regions, edited and softer at the margins. Ivory, midnight indigo, dusky violet, mineral jade, muted coral, champagne. Distinct individual art direction, no generic fantasy castle wallpaper. No lettering, interface, logos, books, scattered stars or glitter, no jewel-encrusted ornament, no neon rainbow lasers, no glossy plastic render, no audience. Wide landscape finished artwork.
